Medical History

  - Symptoms: very itchy, dry, sore; skin cracks present; no weeping; no scratch marks; no thickened/darkened skin reported.
  - No fever or joint pains; otherwise feels well.
  - Past history of eczema and asthma.

Management Plan

- Diagnosed a widespread eczema flare.
- Continue emollients: Diprobase cream and Dermol soap substitute.
- Start fexofenadine (antihistamine); dose not documented in transcript.
- Start Betnovate (betamethasone valerate) topical steroid: apply a thin layer (fingertip unit guidance) twice daily for 2 weeks to affected areas.
- Education: continue emollients alongside steroid; use small amounts; monitor for adverse reactions; contact clinic if worsening or no improvement after 2 weeks or if any adverse reaction occurs.
- Prescription sent electronically to patient’s nominated pharmacy (Boots).
- Follow-up: advised to call earlier if worsening; otherwise reassess in 2 weeks if not improved.

- Missing expected elements: BP, pulse, height/weight/BMI/waist, immunization review, sexual/reproductive history, contraception, pregnancy intentions, physical activity/diet, alcohol use, tobacco use, other substance use, mood/depression screening, hearing assessment, vision screen, oral and ear exam findings, urinalysis, fasting/random glucose, lipid profile, cervical screening status, STI screening, other relevant labs (HbA1c, iron studies, Vitamin D).
- Internal contradictions: Family history—patient stated mother has hypothyroidism; clinician restated as hyperthyroidism (conflict noted). Minor terminology discrepancy: “Diprobase” vs clinician said “diprovate” for emollient (unclear if same product).
- Transcript quality: Sections contained pauses, incomplete/unclear words, and minor audio clarity issues; some medication names/doses were not clearly stated.
